Our security team has two high-level asks before we sign the PO: 1) exact outbound endpoints/IP ranges Redwood needs to reach (control plane + health checks), and 2) recommended egress architecture for on-prem deployment where we must route all external traffic through our corporate proxy and IDS.

Specifics:
- We cannot allow arbitrary outbound IPs from the app subnet; we need a stable list or a proxy destination.
- All TLS must be terminated inside our edge; we will only allow outbound CONNECT to your proxy.
- We need guidance on SNAT, DNS resolution (should we use our resolvers?), and whether mutual TLS is supported.

Attached is a short questionnaire and our procurement timeline (we aim to complete security sign-off by 2026-07-30). Can you send a recommended firewall/NAT pattern and example ip list or proxy URL?

Maya — thanks for the clear list. High level summary up front: we support two deployment egress patterns for Private (VPC/on-prem): 1) Customer-managed egress (recommended for max control) and 2) Redwood-managed egress via our regional proxy pools (useful where customers cannot host proxies). Either approach satisfies your constraints; the tradeoffs are below plus a sample ruleset attached.

Key points:
- Control plane endpoints: 3 stable FQDNs used for control plane calls (api.private.redwood.com, metrics.private.redwood.com, auth.private.redwood.com). We publish short-lived IP ranges for the hosted proxy pool; for full stability use the proxy URL instead of allowlisting IPs.
- Proxying: If you require all TLS to terminate inside your edge, configure an outbound HTTP(S) CONNECT to our proxy (proxy.private.redwood.com:8443) and allow only that destination. We support mTLS to the proxy using certs we will provision and rotate.
- SNAT and source IPs: For customer-managed NAT, you will see SNATed traffic from your NAT gateway. For Redwood-managed egress, SNAT is performed by our proxy pool and IPs rotate within a published set; we provide an IP export 24h in advance for maintenance windows.
- DNS: Use your internal resolver; we recommend split-horizon so internal hostnames resolve locally. For egress to Redwood components, resolve the proxy FQDN inside your network to the proxy IP(s).
- Health checks: health and metrics calls originate from the same control plane FQDNs. We do not require ICMP; TCP/443 outbound to metrics.private.redwood.com is sufficient.
- Logging & auditing: we can emit request-level audit logs to an S3-compatible endpoint or forward via syslog to your SIEM over the established TLS tunnel.

I've attached a CSV with a sample firewall rule set (redwood-private-egress-sample-rules.csv) and an architecture diagram showing both options. Next steps: if you prefer customer-managed egress, please share the NAT IPs you will use and we will lock down token issuance. If you prefer Redwood-managed proxy, we will provision mTLS certs and schedule a maintenance window to seed the IP allowlist.

Cc'ing Lauren (security engineering) and Marissa (account lead) to coordinate certs and legal inputs.

Best,
Priyom Das

Maya — forwarding the options from Priyom. Quick clarifications inline from our SRE playbook: 

> On Mon, 20 Jul 2026 at 09:34, Priyom Das wrote:
> > - Proxying: If you require all TLS to terminate inside your edge, configure an outbound HTTP(S) CONNECT to our proxy (proxy.private.redwood.com:8443) and allow only that destination. We support mTLS to the proxy using certs we will provision and rotate.

Note: if you choose proxy mode and insist on in-edge TLS termination, the typical pattern is: app -> corporate proxy (CONNECT) -> outbound TLS tunnel -> redwood proxy. That preserves egress inspection while keeping control-plane TLS end-to-end. Our recommended firewall rules (attached) show minimal ports (TCP/443 and TCP/8443).

Sample firewall snippet for customer-managed NAT (replace X.X.X.X with your NAT IPs):
- Allow TCP 443 to metrics.private.redwood.com (resolve to FQDN)
- Allow TCP 443 to auth.private.redwood.com
- Allow TCP 8443 to proxy.private.redwood.com (for provisioning & heartbeat)
- Deny all other outbound to 3rd-party ranges except corporate patching CDN ranges you maintain

We can provide an automation script that updates your firewall using a signed token; it requires a single inbound jump from your management network to a Red Team-approved API endpoint. If you'd rather we do not touch your firewall, we can exchange the NAT IPs and add seals to token issuance.

Let us know which pattern you prefer and the target date for cutover.

—Marissa

Redwood Inference
